author: human
request:
Bug report: opening /owners?page=0 — or any page value below 1 — renders the
error page instead of the owner list. Expected behavior: the owner listing
treats any page value below 1 as the first page and responds with the normal
listing (HTTP 200). Find the cause, fix it, and cover the fix with a test.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Owner list treats a page below the first as the first page
summary: Opening the owner list with a requested page number below 1 shows the first page of the normal listing instead of the error page.
acceptance_criteria: given a requested page number of 0, when the owner list is opened, then the first page of the owner list is shown with a successful (HTTP 200) response, not the error page
given a requested page number below 0 (for example -1), when the owner list is opened, then the first page of the owner list is shown with a successful (HTTP 200) response, not the error page
given a requested page number of 1 or above, when the owner list is opened, then the listing is unchanged from today's behavior
non_goals: changing how the veterinarian directory handles page numbers below 1 (not in the quoted request; left open, not declined)
defining behavior for a page number past the last page, or a page value that is not a number (not in the quoted request; left open)
changing page size or any other aspect of owner search
notes: Bug fix grounded in intake line 1 (source: task-prompt, decisions empty); the request itself states the expected behavior and contradicts no recorded requirement or Non-Goals row. PRD edited: REQ-OWN-005 added under Owner records (anchor, one narrative sentence, one Done-when bullet). REQ-OWN-002 is untouched. Observed cause, for the design expert to confirm: the owner search turns the requested page into a zero-based page index without a lower bound, so page 0 or below yields an invalid page request. The case 0 and the negative case are one behavior: one data-driven test. No autofix records to audit.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Covered by docs/architecture-principles.md § Web controller row: normalizing a request parameter to its permitted range is binding, not a business rule, so the clamp belongs in OwnerController. docs/system-design.md § Contracts OwnerController row (now citing REQ-OWN-005) owns the owner search with paging. Cause confirmed by reading the source (grep/read basis, no IDE oracle connected): OwnerController.processFindForm binds `page` with default 1, and findPaginatedForOwnersLastName calls PageRequest.of(page - 1, pageSize). Page 0 or below gives a negative page index, PageRequest throws IllegalArgumentException, and the error page renders. Fix: normalize the bound page to at least 1 once at the top of processFindForm, before both the query and addPaginationModel, so the model's currentPage matches the page actually served.
integration_points: Binding: GET /owners adds no new entry point and no new binding target; `page` stays a request-scoped int @RequestParam and Owner stays bound under the existing setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id") allow-list (docs/security-principles.md mass-assignment row).
Double, framework transport: MockMvc in the existing @WebMvcTest(OwnerController.class) suite, the sanctioned mock per CLAUDE.md Testing Strategy.

Double, repository: OwnerRepository stays the suite's existing @MockitoBean (tolerated per docs/testing-principles.md mocking policy). The test stubs findByLastNameStartingWith with a multi-owner page so the list view renders. It should verify the Pageable passed has page index 0, which shows that page 0 and -1 both resolve to the first page.

patterns.description: request-parameter range normalization is binding and belongs in the controller
existing stubbing of findByLastNameStartingWith with any(Pageable) for list-rendering tests

risks.risk: If only the PageRequest call is clamped, currentPage in the model still shows 0 or a negative number, and the pagination links render wrong.
risks.mitigation: Normalize once at the handler entry and pass the normalized value to both helpers (docs/architecture-principles.md § Web controller: bind, delegate, select).

risks.risk: The owner listing scales with data, and docs/system-design.md has no § Scale and Load section to cite a row from.
risks.mitigation: The slice adds no new data-scaling path: the existing fixed-size page query is unchanged. Use the simplest readable form, a Math.max lower bound. The missing section is a brief gap, recorded in notes.

notes: No design-doc-autofix records to audit. The only design write is REQ-OWN-005 joining the OwnerController Contracts row. Per the prd-entry non_goals, VetController has the identical PageRequest.of(page - 1, ...) pattern and is deliberately left unchanged. This slice does not need a row, so none is written here; a later slice that adds a data-scaling path should seed it.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Boundary validation strengthened, not weakened: OwnerController.java line 97 `int page = Math.max(requestedPage, 1);` clamps the request-supplied page at the boundary before it reaches `PageRequest.of(page - 1, pageSize)` (line 138), so a value below 1 can no longer raise the IllegalArgumentException that rendered the error page. This matches the trust-boundary rule in docs/security-principles.md ('Validate type, range, and shape before use').

No injection reach: the page parameter is still bound as a primitive `int` (line 95 `@RequestParam(name = "page", defaultValue = "1") int requestedPage`), so it cannot carry text into the Thymeleaf preprocessing expressions in templates/owners/ownersList.html (line 44 `th:href="@{'/owners?page=__${currentPage - 1}__'}"`, line 49 `__${currentPage + 1}__`). Those preprocessing uses predate this change and only ever evaluate an integer. Non-numeric input still fails type conversion in the framework, as before.

Upper bound unchanged and safe: a very large page still yields an empty or later page through the derived-query repository method `findByLastNameStartingWith` (parameterized, no string-built query). The change adds no new query path.
No change to binding or mass-assignment surface: the `Owner` binding on GET /owners and the `@InitBinder` `setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id")` (line 61) are untouched, and this handler never saves.

No secrets added: `python3 scripts/changeset.py | grep -i -E '^\+.*(password|secret|token|apikey|api_key|credential)'` returned no lines. No new endpoint, logging, file I/O, or deserialization in the diff (changed files: docs/prd.md, docs/system-design.md, OwnerController.java, OwnerControllerTests.java).

Supply chain: no dependency change (build.gradle is not in the change set). No NVD match ran: dependencyCheckAnalyze is not configured (`grep -i -E 'dependencyCheck|owasp' build.gradle` returned nothing) and this review has no network access. Resolved framework versions: Spring Boot 4.1.1 (build.gradle line 5) and Jackson tools.jackson.core:jackson-databind 3.1.5 (from `./gradlew dependencies --configuration runtimeClasspath`).

semantic_surprise.note: Read the hunk in context: the parameter is renamed to requestedPage with name = "page" so binding is unchanged, Math.max(requestedPage, 1) feeds both PageRequest.of(page - 1, 5) and the currentPage model attribute, values of 1 and above pass through untouched, and even Integer.MIN_VALUE clamps to 1; no guard was weakened and no other branch changes.

test_adequacy.note: The parameterized MockMvc test drives page 0 and -1 through real dispatch and binding, asserting HTTP 200, the list view, currentPage 1, and that the repository is asked for page index 0; it would fail against the unfixed code, which threw IllegalArgumentException.
